newsitem.title: INDIA: German minister says no money for French missiles.
newsitem.headline: German minister says no money for French missiles.

text.p: German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said on Thursday military budget cuts had forced Bonn to cancel a proposed missile deal with France and indicated a possible scaling down of other defence projects.
Ruehe told a news conference in New Delhi that Germany planned to buy 140 Eurofighter combat aircraft being developed by a European consortium, instead of the earlier expected 180.
"We don't have the money for that," Ruehe said, asked if Germany had called off talks with France to buy the French-made Apache air-launched cruise missile for its Tornado combat jets.
"Everybody has budget cuts," Ruehe said. "France has, Great Britain, Germany has. We are in a difficult decision-making process."
Ruehe was speaking at the end of a two-day visit to India, the first by a German defence minister.
He said negotiations over the Eurofighter were continuing.

"Especially the question of money we can use for the Eurofighter in the next four years... I will negotiate until I have satisfactory results. I can only spend the money I have. We need a plane and we want it to be a European plane," he said.
Germany is also finding itself short of money for the Helios II spy satellite project, which Ruehe said he keenly promoted.
"We had come to an agreement. I had myself supported the idea. But at that time I had seven billion Deutsche marks more than I have now, for the next four years. So I have new priorities," he said.

Ruehe has come under pressure recently from the German contractor in the four-country project, Daimler Benz unit Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa), to make a firm order this year for its 180 Eurofighters or risk a cost explosion.

The Eurofighter consortium submitted a sale offer to the German government last spring, valuing each Eurofighter at around 100 million marks ($66 million), but talks are bogged down on price and delivery schedules.
The aircraft's manufacturers have suggested extending the delivery period for the Eurofighter by a year. Ruehe declined to say whether he would accept that proposal.
The Eurofighter is due to be built by a consortium linking Dasa with British Aerospace Plc, Alenia SpA of Italy and Spain's CASA.
